podcast.title: Identity and Origin (1978)
podcast.body: It was later revealed that his real name is Sterling Smith and he is from Houston, Texas, with his releases beginning in 1978 on the Corwood Industries label, which only seemed to have a post office box. "He's been releasing super low five almost unlistenable indie records for years, before we learned that his name was Sterling Smith, and he was from Houston, Texas. These releases started appearing in 1978 on the Corwood Industries label, which only seemed to have a post office box."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "Representative from Corwood" Pseudonym
podcast.body: When not using the name Jandek, he refers to himself as "the representative from Corwood." "when he doesn't go by Jandec, he refers to himself as the representative from Corwood."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Burned Novels Story
podcast.body: A story circulates that Jandek wrote seven novels, but upon their rejection by publishers, he burned them all. "Another story. He wrote seven novels, but when all were rejected by publishers, he burned them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Cult Figure of Outsider Music
podcast.body: Jandek is a cult figure known for creating "outsider music" from Texas, releasing super low-fi and often "almost unlistenable" indie records. "Jandec, the cult figure and creator of what's known as outsider music from Texas. He's been releasing super low five almost unlistenable indie records for years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dedicated Guitar Tuning
podcast.body: Despite the often challenging and seemingly unstructured nature of his music, Jandec reportedly maintains that he carefully tunes his guitar for each and every composition. This detail adds another layer to his unique and enigmatic artistic process, suggesting deliberate intent behind his sound. "And by the way, Jandec maintains that he carefully tunes his guitar for each and every composition."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Enduring Reclusiveness
podcast.body: Despite these sporadic public appearances and media mentions, Jandek remains a reclusive, mysterious, and unknowable figure, yet an important cult hero to many. "Despite all this, Jandec remains reclusive, mysterious, unknowable, and an important cult hero to many."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Live Performances
podcast.body: The mystery surrounding Jandec began to unravel in 2004 when he performed live for the first time at a festival in Glasgow, though uncertainty persisted about the performer's true identity. Since this debut, he (or someone appearing to be him) has made several live appearances annually. "The mystery began to unravel in 2004 when he performed live for the first time in a festival in Glasgow."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Limited Interviews and Documentary Absence
podcast.body: Only two unauthorized phone interviews with Jandek have ever been published, and although a few journalists tracked him down, they shed little light on him. He does not appear in the 2004 documentary "Jandec on Corwood." "Only two interviews have ever been published, both of them of the unauthorized variety, and they were done by phone. A few journalists have tracked them down, but they did little to shed much light on them. And there was even a documentary in 2004 called Jandec on Corwood, but he doesn't appear in the film."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mention in Outsider Music History
podcast.body: Jandic is listed among artists previously covered as examples of outsider music, alongside Wesley Willis, The Shags, and others. "On those programs, I covered Wesley Willis, the Shags, the legendary Stardust cowboy, Jandic, Captain B. Fart, Daniel Johnson, Florence Foster Jenkins, and even Charles Manson."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mysterious Background and Finances
podcast.body: Little is definitively known about Jandec's background; he is thought to be from Houston, Texas, with indications he was a failed author or a machinist. The source of his funding for recordings and his Corwood Industries label remains unclear, though hints suggest the "Sterling Smith Corporation," sharing a phone number with Corwood, is a stocks and securities company. "Outside of the fact that he was in Texas, no one knew where he was, where he got his money to finance his recordings and his record label and how he supported himself."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Name Origin from "The Units"
podcast.body: The name "Jandec" came about after he was forced to change his original outfit's name from "The Units" because another group was already using it. The story suggests the name originated from a phone call in January with someone named Decker, hence "Jan-Dec." "The name Jandec came about after he was forced to change the original name of his outfit from the units to something else after he learned that another group was already using that name. The story is that it came up with the name Jandec, when in the month of January, he was on the phone to someone named Decker. So Jandec, I guess."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Outsider Music Artist
podcast.body: Jan Deck is identified as an artist who creates outsider music. "outsider music like we get from guys like Jan Deck."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Debut Performances and Media
podcast.body: Since his first public performance in October 2004, Jandek has played on average a couple of shows per year, always with different backing musicians, without promotion or post-event acknowledgment. A film of a Toronto performance exists, and a one-act play featuring Jandek ran on PBS. "Several other appearances followed, all with no promotion and get this, no acknowledgement afterwards that they ever happened. Since then, Jandec has played on average a couple of shows per year, each time with different backing musicians. There was a film of a performance in Toronto and then a one-act play featuring Jandec that ran on PBS."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Prolific and Anonymous Output
podcast.body: Jandek has released approximately 100 albums and DVDs, sometimes up to five per year, none of which include biographical information or more than nonexistent liner notes. His financing was unknown, though evidence in 1986 suggested he might have been a machinist. "Keeping track of Jandec is hard. These release somewhere around 100 albums and DVDs, sometimes up to 5 a year. None have ever come with any biographical information. Dinner notes are almost nonexistent. No one knew who this guy was or what he was trying to accomplish or how he was financing this operation, although evidence emerged in 1986 that he was some kind of machinist, so maybe he had a day job."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Reclusive Nature
podcast.body: Jandec, whose real name is thought to be Sterling Richard Smith, is known for his extreme reclusiveness, often likened to J.D. Salinger. He has never given interviews, answered correspondence, or provided insight into his identity or personal life, maintaining an almost complete aura of mystery around his public persona. "The guy is like JD Salinger. He is unbelievably reclusive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unknown Guest Musicians
podcast.body: Some of Jandek's songs feature guest appearances from other musicians, but nothing is known about their identities either. "Some songs feature guest appearances from other musicians, but nothing is known about them, either."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

concerts.title: Glasgow Festival (2004)
concerts.body: Jandek performed live at a small festival in Glasgow in October 2004, marking what is believed to be his first public performance ever. "In October 2004, he performed live at a small festival in Glasgow. As far as anyone knows, this was the first time Jandec played in public."
